description: We are a group of AUB students willing to monitor the cognitive performance of astronauts
summary:
SpaceFog is a local application that allows astronauts to self-monitor their cognitive abilities while on space missions. 

It provides the crew with a dashboard where each astronaut performs cognitive assessment tests, measuring their speed and accuracy. The application then compares their performance to their personal baseline on a daily basis. Accordingly, the application suggests task reassignment, which only passes if approved by the commander. 

In addition, cabin readings ranging from carbon dioxide to temperature levels, are measured and predicted. Deviations from the normal trigger a flag, requiring astronauts to perform the cognitive assessment again.

Moreover, wearable signals and sleep recordings are collected and coupled with the cognitive test results to produce final scores and recommendations. 

Our goal is simple: safer crews, balanced workloads, and benefits on Earth.
details:
SpaceFog – Astronaut Health Monitoring System

SpaceFog is an innovative application designed to monitor astronauts’ physical and cognitive health during space missions. It aims to improve crew safety and mission performance by continuously analyzing different health indicators, including heart activity and heart rate variability, pulse, oxygen saturation, and respiration signals, alongside environmental data. This helps identify unusual changes and evaluate each astronaut’s overall condition and readiness.

The application combines health monitoring with cognitive assessments, through the PVT, DSST, and F2B tests that measure vigilance, processing speed and working memory respectively, to provide readiness scores and alerts when an astronaut may not be fit to perform a specific task. It can also recommend temporarily placing tasks on hold or assigning a qualified backup crew member to ensure mission continuity and reduce potential risks. All decisions are ultimately reviewed by the commander.

The application is set to a default of four crew members but additional members can be added. At the start of each day, each astronaut logs in to their dashboard and performs the cognitive test. Based on their result and the calcuated risk score, the application suggests a task distribution. Then, troughout the day, cabin readings are performed and predicted every five minutes, and if the measurements exceed the limit, a flag appears, asking the astronauts to take the test again, and assigns a new task arrangement if needed.

Our project uses NASA’s Open Science Data Repository (OSDR), RADLAB, and PhysioNet resources for research and reference. The prototype was developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Python, Google Colab, and Canvas, incorporating both real and simulated data to support monitoring, analysis, and visualization.

The main benefits of SpaceFog are improving astronaut safety, detecting potential health and performance issues early, reducing human error, and supporting informed decision-making during missions. It also helps mission teams better manage crew responsibilities and maintain operational efficiency.

What makes SpaceFog unique is its integration of physical health monitoring, environmental awareness, and cognitive assessments into a single platform. Rather than evaluating each factor separately, it brings them together to provide a more complete picture of astronaut readiness.

Throughout development, our team considered several important factors, including data reliability, individual health differences, accuracy of monitoring, ease of use, response time, and the challenging conditions of space missions. Our ultimate goal is to contribute to safer, smarter, and more efficient space exploration by putting astronaut well-being at the center of mission planning.
